messages:
elaine: Quick usability pass on API keys panel after today's design sync. A few separate notes: bulk disable wording, undo affordance, and empty-state CTAs.
mike: Cool, drop them here and I'll triage.
hari: +1. I prototyped a tiny toast pattern we can reuse for other batch ops.
elaine: 1) Bulk action label: swap 'Revoke' / trash icon for 'Disable' + pause icon. Users associate trash with permanent loss. Since we soft-delete for 30 days, 'Disable' is clearer and less alarming.
zoe: Agree. Also update confirm copy to reflect soft-delete window: 'This will disable selected keys — they can be restored within 30 days.' Primary button: 'Disable keys' (destructive).
mike: Backend note: keys have deleted_at and expiry logic. Frontend should call /keys/bulk_disable and show per-key result.
hari: 2) Undo behavior: propose 10s persistent toast with keyboard-focusable Undo button. For users without restore perms, don't render Undo. Also aria-live='polite' and role='status' so screen readers get it but it's not overly disruptive.
elaine: Make sure toast announces "X keys disabled. Undo" rather than generic text. We'll need copy review.
zoe: 3) Post-bulk details: if some keys fail (org-managed, protected), allow partial success. Show a summary toast that links to a details side-sheet listing per-key status and error reasons. Keep focus trapped in sheet for keyboard users.
mike: I'll implement partial response parsing; API will return success/failure per id.
hari: 4) Empty state: current text 'No API keys' is bare. Suggested: 'No API keys yet — create one to start calling the API. Need a temporary credential? Create an ephemeral key.' Provide two CTAs: primary 'Create key', secondary 'Key types & best practices'. Include a tiny checklist link for rotation best practices.
elaine: Also for the empty state, include a small copy about team permissions: 'Admins can create org keys. Members may need additional perms.' helps reduce support tickets.
zoe: Accessibility nits: ensure the 'Expires in X days' pill is announced as a label, not a button. Use aria-hidden=false with aria-label 'Expires in 20 days' and tabindex=0. But ensure it's not in the tab order if it's not actionable; maybe use role='status' and visually focusable only via skip link? We should decide.
mike: I'd avoid adding it to tab order. Use aria-label on the container and make the entire row announce the expiry.
hari: Edge case: rotating a key during bulk disable. Disable rotate option when status != active and show tooltip 'Enable to rotate'.
elaine: Colors: change full-danger red to a medium-warning for disable modals and badges. Reserve red for permanent deletion screens. Run contrast checks for badge text.
zoe: UX microcopy: modal intro: 'Disabling removes the key from active use. You can restore it within 30 days; after that it will be permanently deleted.' Button copy: primary 'Disable keys' (destructive), secondary 'Cancel'.
ui-bot: Link: design-ux#734 contains mocks and color token suggestions. https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/734
elaine: Action items: 1) update mocks to 'Disable' label + new icon; 2) add 10s undo toast with perms gating and aria-live; 3) implement per-key partial results + details sheet; 4) refresh empty state copy + CTAs; 5) contrast pass for warning badge. I'll open a tiny spec and attach annotated mocks.
mike: I'll pick up the frontend implementation and coordinate with hari for accessibility details.
hari: I'll run an a11y pass and prepare screen reader narration examples.
zoe: I'll finalize copy variants for research.
elaine: Thanks team :sparkles:
